pageContent: An old article has been found printed on a poster from back in 1851, kindly uploaded by our readers, the text is as follows:

1st of July 1851 - The Silver Mine at Black Pine was officially declared 'Exhausted' today after no further seams have been discovered for over two months of digging.  Work is set to dismantle the extraction machinery and rails, and move along to dig out a new extraction shaft, where more seams of Silver Ore were discovered during prospecting.

images.caption: The last day of the Silver Mine at Black Pine, 30 June 1851

pageContent: John Baxley was one of the most distinguished photographers that gave up hours of his time to help our club.  Originally a Police Diver and Photographer, he was famous in his working life for working and surveying the scene for some of the most high profile cases of his time, including but not limited to the infamous unsolved Arnie Spencer Tragedy, as it came to be known.  He joined our club in 1928 following his retirement from the North West Mounties.  Here we can see John in a rare photo with the Mounties Search Party in July 1901 before starting work in the Old Silver Mine at Black Pine, he is normally on the other side of the lens!
